sections.h2: Where is Shelby County, Kentucky, and which towns does it include?
sections.html:
Shelby County lies between Louisville and Frankfort and belongs to the Louisville metropolitan area. It was established in 1792 from land given up by Jefferson County, and its name honors Isaac Shelby, Kentucky's first governor. Shelbyville serves as the county seat. The other incorporated cities are Simpsonville and Pleasureville, and Pleasureville sits partly in Henry County.

The county covers 386 square miles, with 380 of them land. Its high point is Jeptha Knob at 1,188 feet, and Guist Creek Lake offers 325 acres of fishing water. Henry, Franklin, Anderson, Spencer, Jefferson and Oldham counties touch its borders. Besides Interstate 64, the main roads are U.S. 60, U.S. 421, KY 53 and KY 55, and Shelbyville itself sits on U.S. 60 about two miles north of the interstate, which was built in 1960.

Smaller places such as Bagdad, Finchville, Christianburg and Clay Village are unincorporated and fall under county government alone. Shelbyville calls itself the Saddlebred Capital of the World.

sections.h2: How do Shelby County incomes and home values look in the Census data?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 51,243 residents for July 2025, up from a base of 48,113 in April 2020, and 20,391 housing units. Most occupied homes are owned, which shapes both the tax roll and the typical sale.

  • Owner share of occupied homes for 2020 through 2024: 73.9 percent.
  • Median value of those homes: $304,800.
  • Monthly cost of ownership: $1,636 with a mortgage and $549 without.
  • Median rent: $1,033, across 18,484 households of about 2.58 people.
  • Median household income: $82,604, and 9.9 percent of residents living below the poverty line.

Louisville's metro area includes Shelby County, and Shelbyville has three industrial parks on its west side. Both shape who buys here and how far they commute.

sections.h2: What is the history and school picture behind a Shelby County address?
sections.html:
Shelbyville was established in October 1792 at the first meeting of the county court, after landowner William Shannon gave up 50 acres and one free acre for public buildings. The Louisville and Shelbyville Turnpike came in the 1830s, a rail line to Anchorage followed in 1870, and downtown was rebuilt after a large fire in 1909.

  • Shelby County Public Schools serves the county with elementary schools named Clear Creek, Heritage, Painted Stone, Simpsonville, Southside and Wright, plus Marnel C. Moorman School.
  • Middle schools are Shelby County East and Shelby County West.
  • High schools are Martha Layne Collins High School and Shelby County High School.
  • The county is classified wet, so package sales and restaurant drinks are legal under the conditions the state sets.

sections.h2: How does the Shelby County PVA assess real estate?
sections.html:
The Property Valuation Administrator runs a state office that works at county level. Each parcel is valued at its full fair cash value, the price a willing buyer and willing seller would agree on, using January 1 as the date. The PVA does not set rates or take payments. Your bill combines that assessed value with rates adopted by state, county and city governments, school boards and special districts.

Tax ownership is fixed on January 1 as well. A parcel bought after that date still produces a bill in the former owner's name until the next year, although the PVA tries to mail it to the new owner using the recorded deed. New owners who receive nothing should call the Sheriff. The county posts a reminder that a buyer's bill may have gone to the previous owner, and that a seller may still have an unpaid bill in their own name. The PVA can be reached at 502-633-4403.

sections.h2: When are Shelby County tax bills due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
One statewide schedule governs (KRS 134.015). Settling a bill in full by the first of November cuts it 2 percent. Between November 2 and December 31 the face amount is owed with no penalty. A January payment adds 5 percent, and a later one adds 10 percent.

The Sheriff collects the bills. The county's own notice says that after April 15 penalties are added and interest keeps accruing, because unpaid claims are then filed with the County Clerk, who keeps the delinquent tax records. A statutory collection fee is added to delinquent bills (KRS 134.119). The Sheriff's website has a Current Tax Bill Lookup, and the office number is 502-633-4324. Anyone paying someone else's bill, such as a tenant, a lender or a person holding an interest in the property, may do so under KRS 134.119 and can ask to be treated as a transferee.

sections.h2: How can a Shelby County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA. Under KRS 133.045 the real property roll stays open for inspection 13 days from early May, six days a week with one Saturday, and anyone planning an appeal must first ask for a PVA conference. The 2026 inspection period has ended, and the next arrives the following spring.

Bring evidence. Sales of comparable houses close by, a recent appraisal or repair estimates carry weight, and a request without paperwork rarely moves the number. If the conference leaves you unsatisfied, the published notice explains how to file with the local assessment appeals board, and a state level tax appeals board hears cases beyond that.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can Shelby County homeowners claim?
sections.html: All property is taxable unless the Kentucky Constitution exempts it, and the main relief for homeowners comes through the Homestead and Disability Exemptions. The PVA takes the formal application, and no exemption exists until one is on file. Ask that office for the current exemption amount and eligibility rules, because the rules can change from year to year.

sections.h2: How should property tax be handled when a Shelby County house sells?
sections.html:
Buyers and sellers commonly split the year's tax at closing, and any unpaid balance is cleared from what the buyer pays. Look up the bill on the Sheriff's website prior to signing, so you know whether an earlier year is still open. The Clerk handles deed recording and takes the seller's deed tax of $0.50 per $500 block (KRS 142.050). A deed at the county's typical $304,800 value owes $305.00, since 610 blocks are counted.

sections.h2: How can a seller handle a Shelby County house with back taxes?
sections.html: A listing, a sale on your own and a cash offer all work when taxes are owed, because the balance gets paid at the closing table. Each route starts with a current payoff figure from the Sheriff. A cash buyer can usually price in the amount owed and skip the lender's repair and appraisal steps.

faqs.q: When are Shelby County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Settle everything by the first of November and the bill shrinks 2 percent; the printed amount holds through December 31. January adds 5 percent, and later payments add 10 percent. The county says penalties and interest build after April 15.

faqs.q: Who gets the bill if a Shelby County house changes hands mid-year?
faqs.a: It goes out in the name of the January 1 owner. A buyer who gets nothing should call the Sheriff at 502-633-4324 or use the online bill lookup.

faqs.q: Where can I check a Shelby County tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the Current Tax Bill Lookup on the Sheriff's website, or call the Sheriff's Office. The office is at 501 Main Street in Shelbyville and serves walk-ins on weekdays, 8:30 to 4:30, holidays excepted.

faqs.q: What does it take to claim a homestead exemption in Shelby County?
faqs.a: File a formal application with the Property Valuation Administrator. The county says no exemption can be granted without one. Call 502-633-4403 to learn the current age or disability requirements.

faqs.q: What deed tax does a Shelby County seller owe?
faqs.a: Fifty cents on each $500 of price, counting a partial block as a full one. A $304,800 sale owes $305.00, and the County Clerk takes the money at recording.
